statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. An operation sequence is a finite ordered list σ = (s_0, ..., s_{k-1}) with k ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ s_t ≤ n-3 for every t < k; its length is k. For 0 ≤ j < n, let c_j(σ) be the number of t < k with s_t ≤ j ≤ s_t+2. Say σ makes all elements 1 if for every j with 0 ≤ j < n, c_j(σ) mod 2 = 1 - nums[j]. Then: (a) if some operation sequence makes all elements 1, r is the least length of any such operation sequence (so r ≥ 0); (b) if no operation sequence makes all elements 1, r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 3 ≤ n ≤ 100000 and, for every i with 0 ≤ i < n, nums[i] = 0 or nums[i] = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs) on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 3 ≤ n ≤ 100000 and, for every i with 0 ≤ i < n, nums[i] = 0 or nums[i] = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r ≠ -1, there exists an operation sequence σ = (s_0, ..., s_{r-1}) of length r (so 0 ≤ s_t ≤ n-3 for all t < r) such that for every j with 0 ≤ j < n, the number of t < r with s_t ≤ j ≤ s_t+2 is congruent to 1 - nums[j] modulo 2. In words, some sequence of r operations makes every element equal to 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 3 ≤ n ≤ 100000 and, for every i with 0 ≤ i < n, nums[i] = 0 or nums[i] = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r ≠ -1, no operation sequence of length less than r makes all elements 1.
